newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt says strikes rich gold deposits.
newsitem.headline: Egypt says strikes rich gold deposits.

text.p: Egyptian government geologists have struck gold in a range of hills on the border with Libya in what the chief geologist called a world class discovery.

"There is no other discovery like this in Egypt. In fact it could be considered a rare discovery on the world level," Gaber Naeim, chairman of the Geological Survey of Egypt, said in an interview published on Thursday.
The gold is in Jabal Kamel, a rocky outcrop close to the point where the borders of Egypt, Libya and Sudan meet, he told the government newspaper al-Akhbar.
The Geological Survey sent geologists to the area to look for iron ore deposits but were surprised to find that there was more gold than iron in the rock, he said.

"The idea was that the gold could cover part of the large costs of exploiting the iron ore and transporting it out of this remote area. But it later became clear that the gold was fundamental and the iron was subsidiary," Naeim said.
"We found we were dealing with (amounts of) gold compared with which the iron was insignificant...So the area really is for mining gold," he added.
Naeim gave no figures for the concentration of gold in the 185 samples his department has taken in two seasons of exploration. He was not available to give further details.
But he added in the interview: "The results showed that concentration of gold in the ore is extremely high and that the amount of ore itself is also extremely high."
He said the deposits were in a range of hills 12 to 13 km (seven to eight miles) long and 10 km (six miles) across. The seams are between four and 75 metres (13 and 250 feet) thick.
"Under the surface of the earth there is another deposit, the size of which is not yet known," Naeim added.
He said that some of the gold was inside Libya and that Egypt had agreed with the Libyan authorities on joint exploitation of the deposits on the border.
One foreign company, Pharaoh Gold Mines of Australia, is prospecting for gold in Egypt's Eastern Desert and plans to start gold production there in the middle of this year.
Naeim told Reuters in March that six other companies were negotiating for concessions to prospect for gold either in the Eastern Desert or in southern Sinai.
But in the interview with al-Akhbar he said the discovery at Jabal Kamel dwarfed all other gold deposits in Egypt.
